assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative long-run empirical account of inequality that reshaped research, public measurement and debate about wealth and income concentration.
assessment.attribution: Piketty's historical synthesis, Saez's income-distribution measurement and Zucman's work on wealth and offshore holdings form a coherent, complementary contribution.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has generated durable datasets, extensive subsequent research and broad relevance across economics.
uncertainties: Cross-country historical wealth and tax data require consequential harmonisation choices.
The proper boundary between the central measurement contribution and broader policy claims remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel methods made credible analysis of persistent economic processes feasible in a vast range of empirical applications.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are tightly associated with the foundational estimators and their practical development.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been established, widely taught and extensively stress-tested over several decades.
uncertainties: Applied work can be sensitive to instrument proliferation and specification choices.
Credit for the broader GMM tradition extends beyond the proposed group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work supplied an influential empirical framework for understanding how technology, trade exposure and tasks change local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide the most coherent core for the task and trade-shock evidence; Katz is an important related contributor.
assessment.maturity: The findings have prompted a large literature and remain central to analysis of structural change.
uncertainties: The relative causal contributions of trade, automation and other concurrent changes remain difficult to separate.
The candidate framing joins several related literatures with partly distinct credit lines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed the modern analysis and measurement of international trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the pivotal framework, with Helpman and Redding making major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in trade research and has been tested across countries and sectors.
uncertainties: The intellectual lineage includes additional foundational trade theorists.
Quantitative estimates of aggregate gains depend on model structure and market assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their systematic long-run comparison of financial crises, sovereign debt and default made historical evidence central to macro-financial analysis.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are clearly identified with the cross-country historical database and its influential synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The agenda has had lasting influence on research and policy discussion, especially following global financial crises.
uncertainties: Some empirical claims associated with the work have faced prominent criticism regarding data construction, coding and interpretation.
Historical comparability across episodes is intrinsically limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy research on institutions, accountability and fiscal capacity has clarified fundamental determinants of state performance and development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini have each made foundational, mutually reinforcing contributions to the field.
assessment.maturity: The body of theory and empirical work is extensive and has shaped research across economics and political science.
uncertainties: The candidate combines several institutional mechanisms rather than one sharply bounded discovery.
Causal identification of institutional effects remains challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and revealed powerful geographic and institutional variation in opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman form the central collaboration behind the data-driven mobility programme; Katz made important connected contributions.
assessment.maturity: The datasets and methods have been replicated, extended and widely used in research and policy analysis.
uncertainties: Mobility measures do not by themselves identify all mechanisms behind observed place effects.
Administrative-data coverage and linkage decisions can affect comparability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a powerful quantitative account of how distortions in the allocation of inputs across firms can affect productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are central contributors to the theoretical framework and its cross-country application.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a substantial empirical and quantitative literature over many years.
uncertainties: Measured dispersion in marginal products can reflect measurement error or adjustment frictions as well as distortions.
The size of implied productivity gains is model-dependent.
